title: Breakpoint types and stepping
purpose: Choose the breakpoint type that answers your question, and choose how to step once the code is paused.
summary: A short deck asks which breakpoint to set for a bug. The main path compares line-of-code, conditional, logpoint, DOM change, XHR/fetch and event listener breakpoints, then the three stepping buttons. Two deep dives show how a conditional breakpoint catches the stale search response and how step into, over and out move through render.
explanation: Each breakpoint type answers one question: where in the code, under which condition, on which element, on which request or after which event. Stepping then moves one line or one function at a time.

learning_check.question: You want to log a value on every call without pausing and without editing the code. Which breakpoint type do you use?
learning_check.answer: A logpoint. It logs a message to the Console and does not pause.

slides.heading: Which breakpoint do you set?
slides.notes: Ask the learner what they know about the bug: the line, the element, the request URL or the event. The answer chooses the breakpoint type.

visual.subtitle: Start from what you already know

slides.heading: One type per question
slides.notes: Reveal the types one at a time. Each one pauses on a different kind of event, so each answers a different question.

items: Line-of-code: pause on an exact line
Conditional: pause on a line only when true
Logpoint: log to the Console, no pause
DOM change: pause on code that changes a node
XHR/fetch: pause when a URL has a string
Event listener: pause on code after an event

slides.heading: Three ways to step
slides.notes: Once paused, choose how far to move. Step over skips a function that is not related to the bug; step into enters one that is; step out finishes the current function.

right.label: The function is not related
items: Step out: finish it and return

visual.verdict: Resume runs until the next breakpoint.

slides.heading: Pause, read, move
slides.notes: At every pause read Scope for local values, Watch for your own expressions and the Call Stack for how the code got there.

visual.verdict: Evidence first, then the next step.

slides.heading: A line breakpoint pauses every time
slides.notes: On line 5 a plain breakpoint pauses for the fresh react response and for the stale re response, so you resume past pauses you do not need.

slides.heading: A condition skips the fresh pause
slides.notes: Right-click the line number, choose Add conditional breakpoint and enter query !== input.value. DevTools now pauses only on the stale response.

slides.heading: Step into render
slides.notes: Paused on line 5, step into moves the pause to line 8 inside render. The Call Stack now has render on top of onInput.

slides.heading: Step over, then step out
slides.notes: Step over runs line 8 and line 9 one at a time; the label then says Results for re. Step out returns to onInput on line 6.

items: Step over: line 8 writes the re items
Step over: label says Results for re
